---
title: "Micronutrients And Omega-3 Pufas To Promote Healthy Ageing: Informing A Physiology-Based Complementation Strategy"
description: Optimizing intake of essential micronutrients and omega-3 fatty acids can counteract age-related declines in organ function, mitochondrial health, and immune response, thereby promoting healthy aging.
author: Gemini
date: 2026-08-03
categories: [Lever, Aging Pathway]
---
As the global population ages, we face increasing challenges with chronic diseases, reduced physical abilities, and loss of independence. Our bodies naturally begin to show a decline in organ function around our fifties. A significant factor contributing to this biological aging process is often a lack of essential micronutrients, which are vitamins and minerals our bodies need in small amounts to function properly.

These micronutrients, including vitamins B, C, D, E, iron, selenium, and zinc, are vital for many bodily processes. They are particularly important for maintaining healthy mitochondria, which are like the powerhouses of our cells. When mitochondria don't work well (a condition called mitochondrial dysfunction), it leads to increased cellular damage from unstable molecules (oxidative stress), chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging), and a weakened immune system (immunosenescence), all of which accelerate aging.

Similarly, many older adults have low levels of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, specifically EPA and DHA, which are known for their anti-inflammatory properties. These beneficial fats work together with micronutrients to help control inflammation in the body.

Emerging research suggests that correcting these deficiencies, perhaps through targeted supplementation, can help restore mitochondrial function and support healthy aging. It's important to remember that these nutrients don't act alone; they work as a complex network, and their effects can vary among individuals. Therefore, strategies for healthy aging should include optimizing both micronutrient and omega-3 intake, potentially guided by routine health assessments and biomarker measurements to address individual needs.
